headline: Navigating new economic realities - Europe’s outlook in a changing global landscape
description_html: Keynote speech by Dr Joachim Nagel, President of the Deutsche Bundesbank, at the 79th Siemens Bankers Conference, Munich, 13 November 2026.
description_text: Keynote speech by Dr Joachim Nagel, President of the Deutsche Bundesbank, at the 79th Siemens Bankers Conference, Munich, 13 November 2026.

1 Introduction

Dear Ladies and Gentlemen,

It is a pleasure to be with you in Munich today. Over the years, this conference has witnessed many shifts in the global economy. We are living through another profound transition – and that is what I would like to talk about today.

Let me start with the big picture. For a long time, the United States was a driving force behind the rules-based trading order. And China was the world’s factory – supplying goods to the rest of the world at highly competitive prices.

But the balance of economic power has shifted. Economic relations are being increasingly shaped by strategic considerations, particularly in sectors such as technology. Trade flows, too, are shifting along geopolitical lines. And that shift is far from over. Its consequences go beyond trade. They are shaping the environment in which monetary policy operates.

So how can Europe navigate these new realities? Two questions will guide me today. First: how can Europe strengthen its economic resilience without giving up the benefits of open markets and rules-based cooperation? And second: how does monetary policy in the euro area respond to a world that has become more volatile?

Let me begin with the forces behind these changes.
